name: Nigeria
prevalence_note: Nigeria official warnings highlight OTP and SIM-swap vishing around fake 5G or SIM-replacement help, plus phone and message phishing that impersonates banks or other trusted organisations, and high-return investment pitches.
cross_border_note: Calls and SMS are often in English and may appear to come from local mobile numbers or spoofed bank short codes.

scams.name: Fake 5G or SIM-replacement OTP vishing

red_flag_keywords.text: asks the listener to recite a one-time password just received
presses for an immediate 5G SIM upgrade over the phone
claims to be a network agent and solicits the activation code

scams.signals_en: A caller or SMS posing as a network or registration agent offers to finish a 5G upgrade or SIM replacement and then asks the customer to dictate a one-time password that just arrived on the handset.
scams.legit_en: NCC consumer guidance and EFCC alerts say genuine SIM replacement is done in a controlled operator or licensed-agent setting; staff should not collect an activation OTP over the phone to complete a remote upgrade.
bait_tactics: The SMS inbox on this MTN line has not shown any new one-time password yet, so I cannot read a code I have not received.
The network settings screen on this handset is still spinning and the upgrade menu will not open.
My reading glasses are in the other room and the message on this small screen is too blurry to read aloud.

scams.name: Bank or service-provider phishing and vishing
scams.name_en: Bank or service-provider phishing and vishing

red_flag_keywords.text: solicits the internet-banking password under a confirmation pretext
asks the customer to speak the token shown in the banking app
instructs a transfer into a so-called safe account

scams.signals_en: Fraudsters pose as a bank or other trusted organisation by email, text or phone and try to harvest passwords, card data or tokens, often with a story about a suspicious debit or an urgent account update.
scams.legit_en: The Central Bank of Nigeria tells customers not to hand over personal or financial information from unsolicited messages and to verify the sender by contacting the institution through a channel the customer already trusts.
bait_tactics: The GTBank app is spinning on this weak signal and the transaction history page will not load, so I cannot see the debit you described.
This token device is in my closed bag in the next room and I am not going to recite a code I have not looked at.
The home Wi-Fi dropped mid-login and the banking app is asking me to start again from the splash screen.

scams.name: High-return investment or crypto pitch

red_flag_keywords.text: urges an immediate starter transfer into the scheme
requires an activation fee before any supposed investment

scams.signals_en: Callers or messages promise unusually high returns with little risk, often dressing the pitch as a crypto pool, trading mentorship or a private placement that needs a quick opening payment.
scams.legit_en: CBN fraud-awareness guidance warns that investment scams dangle quick profits and tells people to research thoroughly, treat get-rich-quick claims with caution, and consult a qualified adviser before sending money to an unfamiliar scheme.
bait_tactics: I have no unused naira sitting in this account for a starter transfer, and I do not fund schemes I have not checked with someone I already trust.
The investment brochure link you sent will not open on this phone, and I am not installing a new app from a chat message.
My salary wallet is already allocated this month, so there is no spare balance for an activation payment.
